facts.text: Plano’s early growth hinged on a road network that linked the outpost to southern Kentucky’s agricultural expansion, drawing pioneer families in the late 1800s.
The origin of Plano’s name remains uncertain, though some suggest a link to Plano, Texas, and a local store that moved closer to Bowling Green in the 1890s.
Plano Elementary School, whose teams are called the Panthers, serves the community’s children.
Freeman Park, a seven‑acre space donated by the Freeman family in the 1950s, offers volleyball courts, a walking trail, and picnic shelters.
Plano emerged in the early 19th century as part of Warren County’s pioneer wave, with farmers moving in after the county split from Logan County in 1797.
By the 1830s, Plano Baptist Church—originally Union Church—was formed with 29 members, reflecting the growing spiritual needs of early settlers.
